findings.title: Blocked email lookup and uniqueness are not normalized
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? queries the exact email string, and the model does not downcase or strip the address before validation or storage. If an admin blocks bad@example.com, a signup using Bad@Example.com, or the same address with surrounding whitespace, will not match and will bypass the block. The uniqueness validation and database index are also case-sensitive, allowing duplicate blocked rows that differ only by case. Normalize emails before saving and querying.

findings.title: Domain whitelist regex is not anchored and can be bypassed
findings.body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds a case-insensitive regex of the form @(domains) without anchoring the domain to the end of the address and escapes only dots. With a whitelist of example.com, an address such as user@example.com.evil.com matches the regex and is accepted, defeating the whitelist. The same pattern can also overmatch blacklisted domains. Parse the domain list explicitly, escape regex metacharacters, and anchor each allowed or blocked domain.

findings.title: should_block? writes statistics during validation and can double-count
findings.body: should_block? loads a BlockedEmail row, increments match_count in Ruby, and saves it while being called from an ActiveModel validator. In UsersController#create, user.valid? is called and then user.save runs validations again, so one signup attempt can increment the same blocked-email row twice. The read-modify-write is also non-atomic, so concurrent requests can lose increments. Move counting out of the predicate or use an atomic counter update once per request.

findings.title: Blocked email specs do not cover normalization or controller integration
findings.body: The specs only exercise exact-case matches, and the validator spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? rather than testing the real flow. There is no test that a User save is rejected when a blocked email is supplied with different casing or whitespace, nor a request/controller test that the signup endpoint actually blocks creation and returns the expected error. Add integration-level coverage for these paths.
